sentences.text: Ruyangosaurus is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur found in the Early Cretaceous Haoling Formation of China.
This animal is characterized by the shape of its vertebral laminae and a robust tibia measuring 127 centimeters in length.
Ruyangosaurus giganteus is considered one of the largest sauropods in China, reaching around 30 meters in length.
The type species Ruyangosaurus giganteus was described in 2009 by Lü Junchang and colleagues.
Ruyangosaurus fossils were recovered from the Mangchuan Formation in Ruyang County, Henan Province, China.
The original describers assigned Ruyangosaurus to Andesauridae, but this family is no longer used because it is not monophyletic.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Ruyangosaurus as Euhelopodidae.
Ruyangosaurus lived in the middle Cretaceous, approximately 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian, in what is now Asia.
Ruyangosaurus lived during the Aptian to Albian stages, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
It is debated whether Ruyangosaurus is a somphospondyl or a non-titanosauriform macronarian closely related to Yunmenglong, as different phylogenetic datasets yield conflicting results.
A smaller phylogenetic dataset based on additional material from the type locality found Ruyangosaurus to be a non-titanosauriform macronarian.
